hero.title: STUDY MBBS IN KYRGYZSTAN
hero.subtitle: Explore MBBS Opportunities in Kyrgyzstan 2026–2027. Pocket-friendly tuition fees, safe campuses in Bishkek, and dedicated Indian hostels.

overview: Kyrgyzstan is the most cost-effective study destination for Indian medical aspirants. Located in scenic Central Asia, medical universities in Bishkek, Osh, and Jalal-Abad offer direct admissions, English-medium lectures, and extensive FMGE/NExT preparation modules.

universities.name: International Medical College
universities.desc: International Higher School of Medicine (IHSM), premier international institute in Bishkek.

universities.name: Kyrgyz Russian Slavic University
universities.desc: Top-tier joint Kyrgyz-Russian government university with high academic rankings.

universities.name: Jalal-Abad State Medical University
universities.desc: Highly affordable government medical academy with large Indian student batch.

universities.name: Asian Medical Institute
universities.desc: Known as ASMI, offering dedicated Indian food mess and FMGE mentorship on campus.

universities.name: Osh State University
universities.desc: Historic state university in southern Kyrgyzstan with 25+ affiliated teaching hospitals.

universities.name: Kyrgyz State Medical Academy
universities.desc: Oldest government medical university in Kyrgyzstan with rich academic heritage.

faq.question: What is the total cost of MBBS in Kyrgyzstan?
faq.answer: The complete 6-year package typically ranges between ₹15 lakh and ₹22 lakh including tuition, hostel, and food.

faq.question: Is Indian food available in Kyrgyzstan medical colleges?
faq.answer: Yes, all major campuses have Indian cooks preparing authentic North and South Indian vegetarian and non-vegetarian food.

comparisonTable.kyrgyzstan: 6 Years (5 years academic + 1 year compulsory internship)
comparisonTable.india: 5.5 Years (4.5 years academic + 1 year compulsory rotating internship)

comparisonTable.kyrgyzstan: Generally smaller batches; high concentration of international students (largely Indian, South Asian)
comparisonTable.india: Large batch sizes (typically 100 to 250+ students per medical college)

comparisonTable.kyrgyzstan: Recognized by NMC, WHO, WDOMS, FAIMER, ECFMG
comparisonTable.india: Recognized globally (NMC, WHO, WDOMS, FAIMER, etc.)

comparisonTable.kyrgyzstan: Offered in English (though basic local language like Russian/Kyrgyz is needed for patient interaction)
Separate hostels with Indian mess facilities available; costs around ₹1,80,000 – ₹2,00,000/yr
comparisonTable.india: On-campus or local hostels/mess; varies widely by college (₹50,000 – ₹1,50,000/yr)

comparisonTable.kyrgyzstan: Annual medical insurance + visa/extension costs roughly ₹20,000 – ₹30,000/yr
comparisonTable.india: N/A (Domestic students do not pay visa/international health insurance)

comparisonTable.kyrgyzstan: Flight tickets (annual), local transit, and living (~$100–$200/month); total course package often lands around ₹18 – ₹35 Lakhs
comparisonTable.india: Low living costs in govt colleges; overall private college investment can scale to ₹50L – ₹1Cr+
